issue_context.title: [Coverity CID :205787] Memory - corruptions in drivers/usb/device/usb_dc_native_posix_adapt.c
issue_context.body:
Static code scan issues found in file:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/master/drivers/usb/device/usb_dc_native_posix_adapt.c

Category: Memory - corruptions
Function: `handle_usbip_unlink`
Component: Drivers
CID: 205787

Please fix or provide comments in coverity using the link:

https://scan9.coverity.com/reports.htm#v32951/p12996.
comments: @finikorg will you be posting a PR for this issue anytime soon?

review_comments: Could You please provide explanation in commit message why skip is necessary here?

I added comment, /* Read USB setup, not handled */
I do not know what really should I add more, the function is self-describing.
Could You please provide explanation in commit message why skip is necessary here?

I added comment, /* Read USB setup, not handled */
I do not know what really should I add more, the function is self-describing.
It the padding (L227) still necessary?
Yes, it is needed
It the padding (L227) still necessary?
Yes, it is needed
It is confusing, I would not expect the function (usbip_send_common) return bool here, what is the benefit to have bool instead of int?
We could return number of bytes written or -1 but we need to check that we wrote exact number of bytes. The true indicates that there is no error and exact packet size is sent.

Could you explain why "true" indicates no error?

`usbip_send_common()` delegates to `usbip_send()` which delegates to POSIX `send()`, which returns the number of bytes written or -1.  The check here is wrong for errors (would convert to true), and potentially wrong for partial success (from which recovery might not be possible).

I believe this should be a compare against `sizeof(usbip_submit_rsp)` in the way things are currently implemented.
Never mind: I had missed the change to the signature.  It'd be nice if error codes associated with the underlying send could be preserved, but this isn't wrong.
